key_terms: The input distribution, query or update pattern, freshness target and failure contract that a capacity comparison must state.
A CPU or memory budget set for safety. It bounds a container but is not measured usage or a production sizing recommendation.
Whether caches, compiled code and materialized inputs were already present when a measurement started.
Choosing among embedded, batch, streaming and serving systems by workload needs and operating cost rather than a single timing.

worked_examples.title: Measure one bounded run with its definition
worked_examples.code:
import time

values = list(range(200_000))
start = time.perf_counter()
total = sum(value * 2 for value in values)
elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
print(total, "elapsed seconds above zero:", elapsed > 0)
worked_examples.interpretation: The printed total is deterministic, while the elapsed time varies per machine, so only its existence is printed here. A capacity claim needs the input size, the timer used, what was inside the timed region and how many samples were taken. One run of a small fixture cannot predict a cluster's throughput; it only gives a baseline for comparing two configurations on the same machine.

worked_examples.title: Container limits versus observed use
worked_examples.interpretation: The output prints each container with current CPU percent and memory used over its limit. The limit is a configured ceiling, not a measurement of need; a container at 30 percent of its memory limit during a tiny fixture says little about production. Sample during the workload, record the sampling window, and keep forecasts in a separate section from what was observed.

evidence: A selected actual supported path with independent source/result/failure/lifecycle evidence; combined topologies and prepared native-server alternatives require separate acceptance and are not inferred from component tests.
